title: Strict-local exchange for abelian coefficients
statement: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let X prime → X, X → Spec A and X prime → Spec B be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. For any abelian etale sheaf G [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] on X and q ≥ 0, the closed B-point stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] of H^q(g^* Rf_* G[0]) and H^q(Rf prime_* g prime^* G[0]) admit additive equivalences with Sheaf.H G q and Sheaf.H (g prime^* G) q [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], under which the stalk of derivedBaseChangeMapPlus [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is cohomologyMap g prime G q [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. No module coefficient category is involved.

source.place: Tag 03QO, and Tag 095T final map-on-stalks paragraph, specialized to strict-local bases before closed-fibre comparison.

proof.text: Use the natural strict-local germ isomorphism and exactness of stalks. Locality puts the image of the closed B-point at the closed A-point; inverse-image stalk comparison and invariance under separably closed residue extensions identify the source stalk with the closed A-stalk.

Choose an injective abelian resolution of G and an injective replacement of its exact inverse image. Apply direct images and the exact closed-point stalks. The strict-local germs identify the resulting complexes with sections on X and X prime; derived global sections compute Ext from the constant integer sheaf. Homotopy invariance gives the two additive equivalences.

Compute derived exchange termwise. The underived mate pulls back sections; after the replacement its homology map is the canonical cohomology pullback. The derived unit description and the constant-sheaf adjunction identify this with the existing Ext map cohomologyMap.
